rationale: THE DOCUMENT-LEVEL CONTRACT for a file the parser cannot fully read, and the fixture that php's `ERROR` claim was MISSING. php's node inventory classifies `ERROR` as `handled_verified` — the analyzer really does handle it (the error-collection walk pushes ParseError rows from a rootNode.hasError walk reading ERROR and isMissing nodes, and the corpus exercises it: two phpunit files are genuine parse errors) — yet not ONE of php's fixture sources produced a tree-sitter ERROR node, so `script/m14/verify-fixture-coverage.ts` read `uncovered: ERROR` and FAILED with 'release blocked'. A handled_verified assertion nobody had ever executed: the same class the grammar-driven construct census was built to find. The sibling lanes that claim ERROR handled WITHOUT a ruling all ship an error fixture — html/error-recovery.html, html/error-budget-broken.html, toml/malformed-and-rejected.toml, svelte/error-recovery.svelte — and php was the only one of the four that did not. THE OBLIGATION is their three-part contract: (1) the broken region is REPORTED as a diagnostic; (2) it is NOT turned into a symbol or an edge, because an ERROR node names nothing a consumer can navigate to; (3) the declarations AROUND it still publish, INCLUDING THE ONES AFTER IT — degradation is PARTIAL, not total. Part (3) is the row that carries the weight, and it is why `After` and `survivesAfter` are written BELOW the broken statement on purpose: a walk that stopped at the recovery node would publish `Before` and nothing else, and the file would still LOOK analysed because `Before` is right there. The broken shape `$b = ;` is not invented — it is verbatim the pinned corpus's own tests/end-to-end/code-coverage/_files/parse-error/src/CannotBeParsed.php, so the fixture exercises a shape a real php file contains. `Broken::m` additionally pins that a method whose BODY fails to parse still publishes as a symbol and as a `contains` edge: the declaration itself is well-formed even when its body is not. ON THE ERROR COUNT: the position and severity are pinned exactly, but the COUNT deliberately is not. One ERROR node yields TWO diagnostics at the same position with the same severity — one from the engine's tree-level pre-pass ('Syntax error (unexpected node)') and one from the analyzer's own walk ('Syntax ERROR detected.'). That is faithful, not duplicated: two independent readers report the same broken region. Pinning a count would freeze an accident of how the engine and the analyzer each phrase a diagnostic, which is not a contract anything should depend on — the contract is that the region is reported AT THAT POSITION.

expectErrors.comment: The broken region IS reported. `$b = ;` at line 66 col 12 — the `=` with no right-hand side. Two independent readers report it (the engine's tree pre-pass and the analyzer's own ERROR walk) at the same position with the same severity, which is faithful rather than duplicated; the fixture pins the position, not the count.

the broken statement `$b = ;` assigns to a name with no right-hand side: there is no callee to call, so no `calls` edge may be invented for it. This is the R10 target-spelling rule holding on a malformed file, where a naive reader would publish the assignment target as a call.
